slot.brief: Hydrogen atom electron jumps from a stated higher level to a lower one; find the emitted photon's energy or wavelength using the Bohr energy-level formula.

stem: In a hydrogen atom, an electron makes a transition from the $n=4$ level to the $n=2$ level. The energy of the emitted photon is:
working:
$E_\gamma=13.6\left(\dfrac{1}{2^2}-\dfrac{1}{4^2}\right)\text{eV}=13.6\times\dfrac{3}{16}\text{eV}=2.55\ \text{eV}$.

Independent check: Photon energy = 13.6(1/2² − 1/4²) eV = 2.55 eV.
solution:
For a transition from $n_i=4$ to $n_f=2$, the emitted photon energy is
$$E_\gamma=13.6\left(\frac{1}{n_f^2}-\frac{1}{n_i^2}\right)=13.6\left(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}\right)=2.55\ \text{eV}.$$

draft.stem: In a hydrogen atom, an electron makes a transition from the $n=4$ level to the $n=2$ level. The energy of the emitted photon is:
draft.distractor_notes: A: uses the binding energy at $n=4$; B: uses the $n=3$ to $n=2$ transition; D: uses the binding energy at $n=2$.
